root_cause.text: Missing validation of individual TCP option length fields in user-supplied fingerprints during addition via nfnl_osf_add_callback(), allowing zero-length options or invalid MSS lengths that cause null-pointer dereference (when foptsize sums to zero and ctx->optp is NULL) or out-of-bounds reads in nf_osf_match_one().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a loop in nfnl_osf_add_callback() to check each option length: "if (!f->opt[i].length || f->opt[i].length > MAX_IPOPTLEN)" and "if (f->opt[i].kind == OSFOPT_MSS && f->opt[i].length < 4)". The CVE description details the null-ptr-deref from zero-length options and out-of-bounds reads from MSS length < 4, both of which were previously unchecked.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prepare the nfnl_osf_add_callback function with new variables for upcoming option length tracking and iteration.
intent_record.what: Added two local variable declarations: unsigned int tot_opt_len initialized to 0, and int i.
intent_record.how: These variables are declared but not yet used in the shown hunk; they prepare the function for future code that will track total option length and perform loops.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add input validation for fingerprint options in netfilter OSF to ensure each option length is valid and total options size does not exceed maximum, and MSS option has proper minimum length.
intent_record.what: Added a for loop after opt_num check that validates each option's length (non-zero and <= MAX_IPOPTLEN), checks that if kind is OSFOPT_MSS then length >= 4, accumulates total option length, and returns -EINVAL if any check fails.
intent_record.how: This change adds runtime validation of the options array in the fingerprint structure, preventing invalid or malicious option data from being processed, which could otherwise lead to buffer overflows or memory corruption.
